response.sql:
WITH site_mesh_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    s.zoneregistry,
    s.entrystat,
    AVG(sm.facetfaces) as site_avg_faces
  FROM sites s
  LEFT JOIN scanmesh sm ON s.zoneregistry = sm.zoneref
  GROUP BY s.zoneregistry, s.entrystat
),
overall_baseline AS (
  SELECT AVG(site_avg_faces) as baseline
  FROM site_mesh_averages
),
status_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    sma.entrystat,
    AVG(sma.site_avg_faces) as status_avg
  FROM site_mesh_averages sma
  WHERE sma.entrystat IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY sma.entrystat
),
kept_sites AS (
  SELECT 
    sma.site_avg_faces,
    ob.baseline,
    sa.status_avg
  FROM site_mesh_averages sma
  CROSS JOIN overall_baseline ob
  JOIN status_averages sa ON sma.entrystat = sa.entrystat
  WHERE sma.entrystat IS NOT NULL
    AND sma.site_avg_faces > sa.status_avg
    AND ob.baseline IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  AVG(site_avg_faces) as avg_of_kept_sites,
  AVG(site_avg_faces - baseline) as avg_excess_over_baseline,
  AVG(site_avg_faces - status_avg) as avg_excess_over_status
FROM kept_sites

assumptions.assumption: The overall baseline is computed over all sites, including those with no mesh records. Sites with no mesh records have site_avg_faces = NULL (no average to compute), which the AVG aggregate ignores per standard SQL semantics, effectively excluding them from the denominator while including the row count implicitly.

alternatives.interpretation: Only sites with at least one mesh record are included in the baseline calculation. This would mean filtering WHERE site_avg_faces IS NOT NULL in both overall_baseline and status_averages CTEs, interpreting 'per-site averages' as applying only to sites that possess mesh data.
